newsitem.title: GERMANY: DePfa reaffirms that UBS has 9 pct stake.
newsitem.headline: DePfa reaffirms that UBS has 9 pct stake.

text.p: German mortgage lender DePfa-Bank AG said on Tuesday it still believed that Swiss banking group UBS has amassed a nine percent stake in it despite UBS's firm denial earlier in the day.

"We continue to affirm that it holds nine percent. We have been told this by a leading independent American firm. Whether the stake is held in its asset management division or somewhere else, we don't know," DePfa spokesman Hanno Strube told Reuters.

UBS earlier on Tuesday denied having any plans to buy up DePfa stock, saying an acquisition of DePfa "would not fit at all" into its strategic plans and said it controlled less than one percent of the bank's shares.

Earlier, DePfa's shares surged as much as 13 percent to an all-time high of 91 marks after the bank said enquiries by an independent firm indicated UBS had bought a "substantial part" of its capital in the open market.
Confusion set in after UBS's denial and DePfa's shares eased to trade up 8.7 percent at 87.50 marks at 1502 GMT.
Strube said his information was that UBS was holding the shares primarily in Zurich and also in London.
He added that DePfa had not yet received any direct signed communication from the management board level at UBS denying that it had built up a stake.
"There will have to be some talks at board level," he said. No appointment has yet been made for such talks, Strube said.

Although it has generally been overlooked in Germany's recent bout of merger rumour frenzy, DePfa is seen as an attractive takeover target in view of its strength in the European market for public loans and its position as a leading German debt issuer.

Some bank analysts said it could make sense for UBS to take on DePfa as monetary union approaches, although the Swiss bank has set its sights on expanding in the lucrative area of asset management -- a field in which DePfa is not active.
DePfa, short for Deutsche Pfandbrief- und Hypothekenbank AG, has a market capitalisation of about three billion marks and total assets of about 165 billion marks.

The bank refinances itself by issuing debt and issued 32 billion marks in bonds last year. It is Germany's biggest issuer of Pfandbrief bonds -- bonds issued to refinance mortgages or public projects.
Some 60 percent of its capital is widely distributed while the remaining 40 percent is owned by a holding company, DePfa-Holding Verwaltungsgesellschaft mbH.

Analysts said the confusion may stem from an 8.2 percent stake in DePfa held by Swiss insurer Swiss Life. UBS will own 25 percent of Swiss Life if the insurer gains approval for a planned conversion into a listed company on June 30.
